question: What does a gesture's evidence preamble cost, and which part of it may a session carry?

device.model: HUAWEI Mate 60 Pro class device under test
device.note: same device and hdc build as injection-path-comparison.json

method: Each preamble step dispatched as its own hdc client invocation, matching the
descriptor-bound dispatcher's one-process-per-step shape in production.
Shapes A and B interleaved within one loop (12 iterations each) so host load
and device thermal drift land on both rather than on whichever ran second.
Injection is deliberately excluded: it is byte-identical in both shapes, so
including it would only add a shared constant to both sides of the comparison.
finding: The preamble's cost is almost entirely the two property readbacks, because
each is a device round trip. The identity query — the step that actually
prevents acting on the wrong device — is answered by the host-side hdc server
and costs an eighth of what the other two cost together.
So the expensive part of the preamble is not the part that guards against the
ruling: A session carries `read-evidence-model` and `read-evidence-firmware`, and never
carries `confirm-evidence-target`. Every gesture re-reads the identity.
Neither property can change on a device that stays continuously connected:
changing either requires a reboot or a reflash, and both drop the connection.
A gesture that re-confirms the same identity is therefore looking at the same
device in the same state that answered those questions. If the identity differs,
or the record has aged past the session lifetime (3600s), the carried facts are
discarded and the device is asked again.
honesty: and each carried fragment records `carriedFromUTC`, the time it was actually read.
This is also the fail-closed mechanism: the hardware-evidence contract admits only
`machineReadback`, so a carried observation cannot be projected as hardware evidence
for anything, and no separate gate has to remember to exclude it.

provenInTests.DiagnosticsAndHAPContractTests.testASess: two gestures through the engine dispatch [observeDevice, evidenceModel, evidenceFirmware, injectPointerInput, observeDevice, injectPointerInput]
provenInTests.DiagnosticsAndHAPContractTests.testACarr: the second gesture still exports a complete observation, named as carried
provenInTests.negativeControl: with the carry path disabled both tests fail, the first with the second gesture re-reading evidenceModel and evidenceFirmware

remainingGap: This removes the preamble's device round trips, not the per-spawn transport cost.
